comment: THE DEAD-CODE FENCE baseline. RE-SEEDED 2026-07-19: the count rose from 0 to 26 and NOT ONE FILE DIED — the instrument stopped reporting a verdict on evidence it never had. Until this re-seed the file fence credited two things that are not calls: (1) ANY quoted string ending in .js became a call edge, matched by BASENAME, so iron-loop-enforcer.js's REQUIRED_LIBS array — a list of paths handed to existsSync — manufactured eight call edges and kept quality-gate.js, v8-dispatcher.js and product-loop.js 'live' on the strength of a presence check; and (2) ANY src/**.js path MENTIONED in ANY markdown became an execution ROOT, bare prose included, so roughly a third of the library was a root because an agent definition described it in a sentence. Comments were scanned too, so a require inside a comment was an edge. The sibling EXPORT fence has always enforced the opposite rule in the same module ('a citation is not an invocation') — the two fences now agree. A path is an edge only when something SPAWNS it; a path is a root only when a shipped instruction RUNS it (node <path> / require('<path>')). This is DEBT that was always there, now visible.
note: DEBT, not blessing. This list may only ever SHRINK; entries leave it by being WIRED to a live root or DELETED. Never add a file here to make a failing build pass. A module is not done when its test passes; it is done when a human can reach it.
whitelistNote: SEPARATE from the debt list above, and conflating the two is what kills a fence. `whitelist` is a PERMANENT exemption for a file genuinely reachable by a mechanism the analyzer cannot see. It maps FILE -> WRITTEN JUSTIFICATION in ONE object (the shape .ctoc/false-green-baseline.json uses) so an entry and its reason cannot desynchronize. It starts EMPTY and is still empty: the one file with a genuine invisible execution mechanism (src/hooks/post-commit.js, run by git after every commit) is declared in .ctoc/reachability-roots.json instead — a declared ROOT is a stronger, more reviewable claim than an exemption.
seedProvenance: Seeded from the analyzer's actual output, not from a number written in a plan. `analyze()` reported readErrors: [] on the seeding run — it read every input it judged. A seed taken from a partial read would be committed debt built on absence of evidence, and this fence's failure mode points at 'everything is dead', so seedReadErrors MUST be 0.
loweredNote: RATCHET DOWN 26 -> 25 (2026-07-21, plan 00120, MEASURED live from analyze()): src/lib/plan-numbering.js is WIRED, not exempted — src/hooks/PreToolUse.Write.js now require()s it to enforce the plan-number collision refusal at plan-create time, so it is reachable from a registered hook root. Its exports are correspondingly live in the export fence (allocatePlanNumber via the start.md create-plan recipe; checkPlanWriteCollision via the Write hook; findNumberCollisions + renumberImplementationPlans via the start.md plan-numbers-check / plan-numbers-repair recipes; the rest via intra-file code edges).
loweredNote2: RATCHET DOWN 25 -> 24 (2026-07-28, plan 00187, MEASURED live from analyze()): src/lib/stale-cleanup.js is WIRED, not exempted — it left the list because the surface-require pattern could not see a require WITHOUT a file extension. src/commands/start.md's cleanup-exec recipe RUNS it via require('{{CTOC_ROOT}}/src/lib/stale-cleanup').executeCleanup(process.cwd(), ...), and Node resolves require('./x') to ./x.js as it always has. The pattern now captures the path with an OPTIONAL extension and credits it to <path>.js only when that file exists in the scanned set, so no edge is invented to a file that is not there. The file was always actively wired; the fence's under-crediting listed it as dead. The skills walk was widened in the same change to collect every .md (not only SKILL.md), making the agent-fragments visible; that credited no currently-unreachable file, because the one citation there (createQuestion in async-choice-protocol.md) is prose, and a citation is not an invocation.
loweredNote3: RATCHET DOWN 24 -> 17 (2026-07-31, plan 00191, MEASURED live from analyze()): the compliance seam's seven-file closure is WIRED, not exempted. agents/coordinator/cto-chief.md's compliance-dispatch section previously NAMED evaluateComplianceTrigger and runComplianceForTransition in prose — a citation, not an invocation — so the reachability fence correctly listed all seven as dead beneath a protocol the coordinator is instructed to follow. The two prose calls are now executable node -e recipes of the menu's literal form, each a require('${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/lib/<module>.js') credited by SURFACE_REQUIRES_RE (and, being node <path>.js, by SURFACE_NODE_RUNS_RE). CTO Chief holds Bash, so it can run them. The trigger recipe roots src/lib/iron-loop-compliance-trigger.js; the seam recipe roots src/lib/compliance-integration.js, whose require edges pull gdpr-agent-runner.js, eu-ai-act-agent-runner.js, compliance-dedup.js, gdpr-helpers.js, and (via eu-ai-act-agent-runner) eu-ai-act-helpers.js. Exactly seven left; measured, not copied. This wires only the seam — the eleven governance controls (ai-provenance, audit-chain, budget, data-lineage, irac-schema, legal-hold, privilege-posture, proportionality, retention, spoliation-safe, traceability-matrix), four-eyes, eu-recommender-helpers, and the rest remain dead pending their own call sites.
